messages.text: What is non-signaling tester, and which product-related measurement decisions depend on understanding it?

The knowledge base gave no validated answer, so the evidence is insufficient for a fully cited answer. It did return partially supported material, summarized below.

A **non-signaling tester** is a tester used for RF measurements without establishing a full protocol-level connection/signaling session with the device under test. In the returned evidence, it is framed mainly as a **production-phase RF measurement approach**: WLAN production RF tests are performed in **non-signaling mode** to save time, and the **R&S CMP180** is positioned for that role.

Product-related measurement decisions that depend on understanding “non-signaling” include:

| Decision | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **CMX500 vs CMP180** | Use **CMX500** for R&D signaling/interworking tests; use **CMP180** for production non-signaling RF tests. |
| **Whether production RF testing should be non-signaling** | Non-signaling mode is used to reduce production test time. |
| **Whether CMP180 fits the production RF scope** | CMP180 is described as a non-signaling RF measurement tester for technologies such as Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7, and 5G NR FR1. |
| **Frequency range configuration** | CMP180 frequency coverage depends on options, e.g. extension from 6 GHz to 8 GHz with **R&S CMP-K168**. |
| **IF bandwidth configuration** | Basic IF bandwidth is 250 MHz; 500 MHz requires **R&S CMP-K185** and related hardware prerequisites. |
| **RF port / MIMO scaling** | CMP180 supports multi-port and MIMO production testing; decisions include 2x2 single-box or scaling to 4x4 with multiple instruments. |
| **WLAN measurement options** | Option choices depend on WLAN standard and test mode, e.g. 802.11a/b/g/n/ac, 802.11ax, 802.11be, and true MIMO options. |
| **Whether wide waveform demos are product requirements** | A 480 MHz WLAN waveform demo was mentioned as a candidate/validation case, not necessarily a formal Wi‑Fi requirement. |

Not from the knowledge base, but generally: the key distinction is that **signaling testing** exercises the device in a network-like protocol session, while **non-signaling testing** directly controls RF transmit/receive behavior for faster, repeatable measurements—especially useful in manufacturing.

data.answer:
已查到可引用的部分資料：

### Short answer
A **non-signaling tester** is presented in the passages as a **production-phase RF measurement tester**: in WLAN device production, RF measurements are executed in **non-signaling mode** to save time, and the **R&S CMP180** is positioned as optimized for that purpose [5]. The key product-related measurement decisions that depend on understanding this are whether to use **R&S CMX500 for R&D signaling / interworking tests** or **R&S CMP180 for production non-signaling RF tests**, and then which CMP180 frequency, bandwidth, RF-port/MIMO, and measurement options are needed [6][3][5][59].
### Product-related measurement decisions
| Decision | What the passages support |
|---|---|
| Choose the right tester role: R&D signaling vs production non-signaling | The Wi-Fi 7 test workflow is split between **R&S CMX500** for R&D signaling / interworking testing and **R&S CMP180** for production non-signaling RF testing [6]. |
| Decide whether production RF testing should be non-signaling | In the WLAN device production phase, **all RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time** [5]. |
| Decide whether CMP180 fits the production RF scope | R&S CMP180 is described as a production-phase **non-signaling RF measurement tester** supporting cellular and non-cellular technologies including **Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7, and 5G NR FR1**, up to **8 GHz** and bandwidths up to **500 MHz** [7]. |
| Decide frequency-range configuration | CMP180 is **6 GHz maximum without R&S CMP-K168**, while **R&S CMP-K168** is the extended frequency range option from **6 GHz to 8 GHz** [3]. |
| Decide IF bandwidth configuration | CMP180 IF bandwidth is **250 MHz basic** and **500 MHz with R&S CMP-K185**, and R&S CMP-K185 is only available if **R&S CMP-B805I or higher** is installed [3]. |
| Decide RF-port / MIMO scaling | CMP180 integrates **two analyzers, two generators, and two sets of eight RF ports** for single-box **2x2 MIMO** testing, and two CMP180 instruments can be combined to support four analyzers and generators for **4x4 MIMO access points** [5]. |
| Decide WLAN measurement options | CMP180 measurement options include **R&S CMP-KM350** for WLAN IEEE 802.11a/b/g/n/ac SISO measurements, **R&S CMP-KM351** for WLAN IEEE 802.11ax SISO measurements, **R&S CMP-KM352** for WLAN IEEE 802.11be SISO measurements, and **R&S CMP-KM360** for WLAN true MIMO 2x2 and 4x4 measurements [59]. |
| Decide whether the 480 MHz waveform demo is a product requirement | CMP180 was to demonstrate loopback validation of a **480 MHz WLAN waveform**, but the source says it is only a potential candidate for yet-to-be-defined Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn and not a formal Wi‑Fi 8 specification [5]. |
